The usual approach is to set A randomly or to populate its columns with samples y (i) . These often work but we do not know how to analyse them. Here we give a novel method for initialization which we show succeeds with very high probability. Our algorithm works by pairwise reweighting. Let u = A∗ α and v = A∗ α0 be two samples from our model whose supports are U and V respectively. The main idea is that if we reweight fresh samples y with a factor hy, uihy, vi and compute p2 cu,v = 1 X M hy (i) , uihy (i) , viy (i) (y (i) )T p2 i=1 then the top singular vectors will correspond to columns A∗j where j ∈ U ∩ V . (This is reminiscent of ideas in recent papers on dictionary learning, but more sample efficient.) Throughout this section we will assume that the algorithm is given two sets of samples of size p1 and p2 respectively. Let p = p1 + p2 .
